recognize_zh: 背景是大量淡色鬼影紅血球（HbA 已被酸洗脫），其間散布一群染成深洋紅色、內部均勻飽滿的紅血球，這些是抗酸的含 HbF 細胞，兩群對比清楚，是 Kleihauer-Betke 陽性的典型畫面。
features: Two distinct red cell populations: numerous pale ghost cells versus scattered intensely eosinophilic, homogeneously stained cells
Darkly stained HbF-containing cells make up roughly one-fifth of cells in this field
Many dark cells are crenated or irregular in outline (preparation artifact)
Ghost cells show only faint membrane outlines with empty interiors
Occasional ghost cell with faint residual granular staining (intermediate cell)
describe_en: Kleihauer-Betke acid elution preparation shows a dimorphic red cell population. The majority of red cells are pale ghost cells in which acid-labile adult hemoglobin has been eluted, while a substantial subset of cells retain intense, homogeneous eosinophilic staining indicating acid-resistant fetal hemoglobin. Several positive cells are crenated, an expected artifact. Findings indicate HbF-containing red cells; in a maternal sample this pattern supports fetomaternal hemorrhage, and the fetal cell percentage should be counted to estimate bleed volume.

ddx.dx: Pancellular hereditary persistence of fetal hemoglobin
ddx.vs: Pancellular HPFH gives uniform staining of essentially all red cells, not a discrete subpopulation among ghost cells.

ddx.dx: Heterocellular HbF elevation (sickle cell disease, beta-thalassemia, pregnancy F cells)
ddx.vs: Maternal F cells tend to stain less intensely and more variably than true fetal cells; flow cytometry with anti-HbF and anti-carbonic anhydrase distinguishes them.
Cord or neonatal blood shows nearly all cells darkly stained, with only few ghost cells.
